column3: One metadata-only event per completed transaction or savepoint, offered from the transactions panel's own recorder at its completion, as BootUI offers it from TransactionRecorder.record (TransactionRecorder.java:315-336, TransactionPayload.java): one tracker, one routing, never SQL text, parameters or URL; produced whenever the transactions recorder runs, independent of SQL Trace; a commit is offered once its DBAPI commit has returned (the panel's settle), so a failed DBAPI commit is the panel's UNKNOWN with rolledBack false and failureClass its exception class (BootUI: status UNKNOWN, failureClass), and a commit never settled (no later begin, rollback or pool checkin on that connection) is not offered; rolledBack is the panel's ROLLED_BACK, so a transaction SQLAlchemy rolls back on close without a commit (a read-only Session, a swallowed IntegrityError) is rolledBack true (BootUI's Spring transactions commit on a normal return, so a read-only Session closed uncommitted reads as rolled back); a connection under AUTOCOMMIT offers no event (each statement commits itself: no physical transaction for BootUI to record), the panel still lists it; nested is a savepoint or another transaction still open in this context (BootUI's thread stack, held weakly: a collected unclosed connection stops counting), while the panel's parentId stays savepoint-only; the panel paused, disabled or suspended (low-footprint) offers no event (BootUI keeps journaling a paused panel); method is the row's call site, or unknown when sql_trace_capture_call_site is off (BootUI's @Transactional method has no Python twin); readOnly only from the postgresql_readonly execution option and isolation only from the isolation_level execution option; rollbackOnly false, ormStatements/ormFlushes/ormDirtyEntities -1 (no W5b orm source yet); not ported: the RuntimeEvent fields executionId, threadKind and failedOrSlow
